question.worked_solution:
To find the second derivative of a vector-valued function, we find the second derivatives of the components.

- For $x(t)=\frac{t}{t-1},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t) & =\frac{(t-1)-t}{(t-1)^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{(t-1)^{2}} \\ {x}^{″}(t) & =\frac{2}{(t-1)^{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

- For $y(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(t) & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t) \\ {y}^{″}(t) & =-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t).\end{aligned}
$$

So, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨{x}^{″}(t),\,{y}^{″}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2}{(t-1)^{3}},\,-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
